why: I checked the PASS and FAIL conditions of both verifier checks against the words of their expect lines. Check 1 passes when the call on invalid JSON "prints `{}`" with no thrown error and src/config.js "catches the JSON.parse error and returns {}". It fails on a throw, a non-empty-object result, or loadConfig not being "in src/config.js". Every one of these comes straight from the expect line. The plain-object test only spells out what {} means. Check 2 is just exit 0 with no failing tests, which is exactly what "npm test passes" means. The stricter items sit under "Advisory (not part of PASS or FAIL)": valid JSON still parsing, a missing file still throwing, how the old test was updated, and the app.js message gap. Neither check has a mutation test, a branch or file-scope rule, or an exact-wording requirement. The criterion holds for the whole output.
